speaker: (the one master)
text: A comedy may end without a marriage. I have said so twice. You have answered twice. Neither of us has become wiser.

speaker: (the other master)
text: It may end, and it will be hissed. An oath that does not reach a wedding is a debt left open on the board.

speaker: (the one master)
text: Then call it a debt. The oath was the play. The wedding would have been a receipt for people who cannot bear an ending.

speaker: (the other master)
text: Receipts are for chambers. You have made a stage into a counting-house, and you want praise for the arithmetic.

speaker: (the one master)
text: I am not asking the man with the cup. He is eating. Eating is an opinion, and it is a quiet one, and I am content with quiet from a stranger.
